body.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). Under \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\), if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)=[L_\delta(b,q,\omega),U_\delta(b,q,\omega)]\subset[0,1/\epsilon]\). Its endpoints are attained by minimizing and maximizing \(\sum_{s,v}\omega_vr_{11v}(s)y_s\) over \(\mathcal C_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). Every optimizer has \(z>0\), maps to \(x=y/z\), and lifts through Theorem \(\text{thm:exact-history-compression}\) to an endpoint-attaining full law.
body.justification: The theorem turns a nonlinear waning ratio into two finite linear programs without sacrificing sharpness or common-law attainability.
body.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give closed-form single-pathogen finite bounds, while Follmann and Huang (2018) use a parametric marked process; neither gives sharp policy-mixture reciprocal endpoints on an LP-certified positive common-history fiber.
body.consumer: A trial analyst can report exact best- and worst-case reference-mixture waning using standard linear-program solvers and attach an auditable latent-law witness.
